title: eDIAR: Training-Free Open-Speaker Streaming Diarization for Long Meetings and Large Archives via e-means
author: Kyudan Jung, Jihwan Kim, Minwoo Lee, Eunji Shin et al.
description: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. summary: Meetings last up to an hour, and nobody knows in advance how many people will speak. Neural diarizers with a fixed number of output slots, such as Streaming Sortformer and Nemotron-3, are accurate and run online, but they cannot name more speakers than they have slots.
takeaways: The slot head keeps deciding who is active and when speech overlaps, and speaker embeddings are clustered inside a single slot, with the official e-means algorithm, only after every slot has been used.
The resulting system has no limit on the number of speakers and stays accurate when speakers outnumber the slots, where fixed-slot models break down.
The method needs little tuning, and e-means runs with its default recipe from a few hundred to more than a million embeddings.
